# Invalidate native lyric sessions and clear OS-facing metadata deliberately

## Platform difference

Native media/lyric surfaces can outlive a Flutter page or hold stale content after the application's track/session changes.

## Implementation

KikoFlu mounts a lyric synchronizer at application scope, queries capabilities and serializes/coalesces writes over its OH lyric channel. A native-session token/epoch invalidates cached writes. Track changes or missing tracks clear previous content; privacy mode hides the native surface before sending empty metadata to reduce transient exposure.

## Applicability

The native implementation is expected in KikoFlu's pinned audio_service fork. This application checkout establishes the caller protocol and privacy ordering, not independently verified system lyric rendering.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

Do not treat hiding a Flutter widget as clearing system metadata. A stale queued update must not repopulate a new/private session. Capabilities and native visibility callbacks are part of the state model.

## Verification

Test track switches during queued writes, native session replacement, privacy toggles, process restart and plugin errors while inspecting the actual system surface.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
